newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end stronger, withstand Dow's slip.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end stronger, withstand Dow's slip.

* Toronto stocks closed within reach of its all-time highs on Wednesday, boosted by climbing conglomerates and banks despite New York's dip. * Almost all 14 sub-indices gained ground.
Toronto's key stock index closed within reach of its all-time high on Wednesday, boosted by conglomerates and banks as investors sought to match Wall Street's recent gains.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index finished 47 points higher at 6307.13, close to its record high of 6348.02 set on March 11.
"We're verging on breaking into new high ground in Toronto," said Ron Meisels, Montreal-based portfolio consultant.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average hit a record of 7382 points on May 14 and surged one percent on Tuesday.
"We're in a bull market," Meisels added. He said that if Wall Street stayed in positive territory "we could have a few up days without any effort."
Wednesday's trading was brisk at 98.7 million shares worth C$1.7 billion.

The conglomerate and utilities sectors led the charge, followed by eight other groups including oils, industrial products and banks. Four of Toronto's 14 sub-indices slipped: retail, golds, consumer products and base metals.
Advancing issues outnumbered declines 551 to 426, while 301 closed flat.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Telecommunications conglomerate BCE Inc, Canada's largest publicly traded firm, rose 1 to 36.

* Tee-Comm Electronics Inc dropped 0.21 to 0.68, losing ground after Wednesday's announcement that Bank of Montreal was reviewing the status of the satellite television provider's demand credit facility.
* Telecommunications firm Northern Telecom Ltd rose 6.40 to 115, topping Toronto's net gainers.
